anyway, i thought the article was fine overall, if a little stagnant. :) good use of redactions at the very end!

"Human subjects who make visual contact with this manifestation hear “whispering” voices, although recording equipment in the area picks up nothing and the phenomenon is observed even in subjects who are deaf from birth."

The pocket is in fact an artificial prison for SCP-305, and it was suggested to me to let people draw their own conclusions about what it looked like. Same with its being Keter-class. I'll think on if I can rewrite it a bit to rearrange it and reduce tl;dr.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I like this concept a lot, and can't help but wonder if the spacetime anomaly is artificial, and actually intended to keep 305 contained. FullHazard's idea to change the designations (305 for the anomaly, 305-1 for the entity inside, 305-2 for its spawn) should definitely be implemented, for consistency with other SCPs such as SCP-076. Other than that, I'd downgrade it to Euclid (it'd be Safe if it weren't for the possibility of escaped child entities on the loose) and trim the article, particularly in those containment procedures. Parts of the containment procedure really belong in addenda, and others are just excessive amounts of detail. Remember, this is supposed to be a quick-reference document for someone who may need to figure out what to do about this SCP in a life-threatening hurry - the most necessary information goes first, and the least immediately-useful stuff comes last (such as in addenda).
